rail_guard.text: Ceannt Station, named for Éamonn Ceannt, who signed the 1916 Proclamation. It's an Irish Rail station, not a Wildlore one, but the rail's the same.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited on this island. Where to?

ring_maker.text: The Claddagh ring: two hands for friendship, a heart for love, a crown for loyalty. Worn heart outwards, it says 'free'. Heart inwards, it says 'spoken for'.
It began in the Claddagh village, a fishing community outside the city walls. Legend says a fisherman, taken by pirates, came back for his love. Whether or not that's true, I sell a lot of them.

hooker_skipper.text: A Galway hooker is a traditional working boat: black hull, red-brown sails, built for hauling turf and fish across Galway Bay.
Four sizes: the Bád Mór, the Leathbhád, the Gleoiteog and the Púcán. I can name them all. I can't sail any of them.

then.text: Grand Aran. My nan says the cables hold the heat. My nan is generally right.
Raining on Eyre Square. The pigeons are fine. I'm late for a lecture and soaked.
Sun in Galway! Half the city's on the grass, the other half is jealous in an office.
Evening already? Shop Street's filling up with buskers. Best show in town, free.

square_student.text: Galway's the City of the Tribes. The fourteen tribes were merchant families, and they ran the place for centuries. Lynch's Castle on Shop Street was one of theirs. It's a bank now. Very respectable.
Eyre Square's park is officially named for President Kennedy, and it's the only place I know where a Kennedy gets less attention than a pigeon.

then.text: Wind's up on the Corrib. The swans are going sideways. Very dignified about it, though.
Fog on the river, so I can hear the swans before I see them. Grumpy wee honks.

busker_swan.text: {greeting} The swans on the Corrib are always the same swans, I'm convinced. They're on a rota. They've got the whole river organised.
The Corrib's one of the shortest rivers in Europe. About six kilometres. It makes up for it in volume.

then.text: Cranes nesting out at Derrygimlagh, they're saying. Cranes! Next you'll tell me the Corrib's running clean.
Rain's good for oysters. Keeps the bay fresh. Keeps the customers inside, mind.
Gale over Galway Bay. Boats are staying in today. The oysters are delighted.
Up at dawn for the boats. The bay's silver this early. Prettiest sight in Connacht.

else.text: {greeting} Galway Bay oysters are the best on earth, and I'd take it to court. September's the Oyster Festival. People wear black tie and eat them with a stout.
Nobody's ever asked me what the oyster thinks. It thinks, 'Why is it me?'

then.text: I've gone full busker. I know three songs and two of them are the same one. A man gave me a tenner for stopping.
Whatever happens at the stones, I'm there. In the back. With a flask. And a very small banner.
The Spanish Arch is lovely, isn't it? There's a swan that follows me. I think it's from the Enclosure. It looks very corporate.
Galway! I've been busking. I made four euro and a sandwich. Living the dream.
Last time before the big one, yeah? Give me everything you've got.

else.text: Nuala's out on the docks. Be nice. She's rowed a currach round the Aran Islands. In a storm. Possibly twice.
I'm going to head down to the quay and look at the Galway hookers. Old sailing boats, red sails. I want one. I can't sail.

gate_galway_north.text: Bog road's closed. The bog is 'in consultation'. It's been consulting for three weeks. It's very thorough.
Keeper Nuala at the docks signs off the paperwork. She and the tide are the only ones who ever finish anything on time.

galway_fisher.text: Heading out from the Claddagh. Night fishing's quiet, just me, the boat and the lighthouse.
Galway Bay by moonlight. The song doesn't do it justice, and the song's very good.
Stars are out over Clare. Grand night for it.

galway_night_fiddler.text: Session's just ended, so I'm playing the last tune to the lamp post. It's a good listener.
Shop Street at night: the buskers gone home, and the stones still humming.
Galway at this hour belongs to the musicians and the seagulls. We share.

isles_bridget.text: {greeting} I'm Bridget, a Traveller. We call ourselves Mincéirí, and we have our own language, Cant. You'll not learn it off me, mind. It's ours.
In 2017 the State finally recognised Travellers as an ethnic minority. My granny cried. She'd been told her whole life we were just settled people who'd fallen on hard times.
Ballinasloe's in October. Horses, cousins, and arguments about both.

isles_rafael.text: {greeting} Bom dia! Rafael, from Goiás in Brazil, and now from Gort, County Galway. In the late 1990s a meat plant in Gort took on Brazilian workers, and now the town has Brazilian shops, churches and some very good footballers.
Ireland spent two hundred years sending people away. Now people come here instead. The Irish understand that better than anyone. Mostly.
I play Gaelic football now too. It's like football, but you can pick the ball up, and everyone is very angry.
